title: TS-40b Switch CloudFront /api* and producers to the ControlPlane, then migrate (development)
description: Part of the flip (chatticus-6f27c5). Infra, development first: CloudFront /api* origin to the ControlPlane FrontDoor Function URL (same behaviors, headers and SSE settings as the current origin; read infra/lib/web-stack.ts and thin-turn-stack.ts), producers (web voice client, schedulers, anything enqueuing to the old TurnJobs and ComputerTurnJobs) to the new queues, then the run order of design 7.1 step 4: preflight, set MIGRATING, bin/migrate-transcripts (dry-run, copy, delta, verify per 2.7), unset MIGRATING. HUMAN GATE: the orchestrator asks the user before this runs, because it moves develop.chattic.us traffic and data. Rollback until day 14 is git revert of the flip commit.

comments.author: home
comments.text: DEVELOPMENT FLIPPED. Sequence run: preflight ok (no active turns, 5 queues empty); migration copy 35 messages in 2 channels, latest-turns 19 converted, verify ok; write gate closed; PR 457 merged (CloudFront /api* origin -> ControlPlane FrontDoor Function URL, MIGRATING write gate wired into the FrontDoor); Web deploy applied; CloudFront Deployed; delta wrote 0, verify ok on both channels; gate opened; acceptance through the public CloudFront URL 9 of 9 PASS (after PR 459: the acceptance client stripped /api from the base URL). Problems found live and fixed: the write gate was never wired into the deployed FrontDoor (found in review before the switch); CloudFormation export deadlock (ThinTurn export still imported by Web) and overlapping workflow runs -> PR 458 orders deploys control-plane, web, thin-turn and serializes each environment with a concurrency group; acceptance client /api prefix (PR 459). State: ThinTurn Python stack still deployed and idle (TS-40c deletes it); Messaging table still owned by ThinTurn (must be retained or moved first). Staging and production are untouched: they switch only at the develop to main promotion, which needs: ControlPlane stacks deployed there (workflows exist), account types confirmed (the thin-turn and web steps use the per-environment scripts; the control-plane step uses the dedicated script, which refuses legacy accounts), and the migration run per environment (gate close, preflight, copy, deploy, delta, verify, open).

right_now_summary: Development traffic and data now use ControlPlane; ThinTurn remains idle while staging and production await promotion.
